description: We are a team of Computer Science students passionate about AI, software development, and space technology. We aim to build innovative solutions using programming, data analysis, and AI tools. We are looking for motivated teammates with skills in AI/ML, web development, UI/UX design, and data analysis who are eager to collaborate, learn, and solve real-world challenges.
summary: Astra Tech is an advanced spacesuit safety monitoring system designed for the NASA Space Competition to protect astronauts by fusing four critical life-support signals into a single, intuitive interface. The project addresses the silent and invisible danger of carbon dioxide buildup, undetected scrubber degradation, unmonitored purge valves, and stress-induced voice changes inside the helmet.   Unlike traditional setups where telemetry data is scattered across separate devices, Astra Tech integrates carbon dioxide levels, scrubber temperature differentials, valve states, and voice integrity into a unified risk score with a clear color-coded display. Operating locally inside the helmet, it provides real-time, multi-severity warnings within fractions of a second—bypassing communication delays inherent in deep space or Mars missions. This solution is crucial because it gives astronauts and flight crews immediate, life-saving clarity, preventing cognitive impairment and physiological risks before they escalate.
details:
• What it does / How it works: Astra Tech is a spacesuit safety monitoring system that continuously reads four critical helmet signals—carbon dioxide concentration, scrubber efficiency (via temperature differential), purge valve state, and voice integrity (stutter detection)—and fuses them into a single, intuitive risk score with real-time, multi-severity alerts. It operates locally inside the helmet to provide instant warnings within fractions of a second.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: The project prevents silent physiological risks and cognitive impairment caused by invisible hazards like $CO_2$ buildup. Its intended impact is to enhance astronaut safety during deep space missions, spacewalks, or Mars operations by eliminating telemetry data overload and bypassing communication delays with ground control.
  • Tools, Languages & Software Used: The interactive prototype was developed using Flutter and Web technologies (under the name AstroPulse).
  • Creativity & Factors Considered: The project is creative because it shifts from scattered, multi-screen telemetry to a unified, human-centric interface that combines physiological and environmental indicators (including voice stress analysis). The team carefully considered critical constraints such as avoiding false alarms, preventing astronaut distraction, and ensuring local processing for deep space environments where Earth communication is delayed.
